# CompPriorityGrid

Sorted into nine bands, not scored on a line.

## When to use it

Fifteen to twenty-five candidates where the scoring is a judgement and the bands are what gets argued about.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | E-comparison |
| Form | matrix |
| Arity | 9 |
| Ground | cream |
| Density | dense, about 560 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | cell at 18px against a 64px headline (ratio 0.28) |

## Why it holds together

The cell is the unit of meaning, not the item. Everything inside one is a peer.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| left-hand inventory | twenty items listed in navy boxes on the left half | dropped | Every item in it also appears in the grid with the same label — a legend for names the grid already spells out. Dropping it gives the grid the full canvas, which is what makes nine cells legible. |
| headline collision | headline overruns into its own OFFERS sub-heading | fixed | A defect, not a style. |

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

## Origin

In the repository its template, `wpp-es-html-deck/canon/templates/comp-priority-grid.html`, is refreshed from this card's preview, and its trace sources (spec, measurements and reference image) are in `authoring/canon-src/comp-priority-grid/`.

# CompPriorityScatter

Everything scored on two axes at once.

## When to use it

Ten to thirty-five candidates to prioritise, where relative position matters more than which box they fall in.

## Shape

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | E-comparison (secondary D-quantitative) |
| Form | matrix |
| Arity | n |
| Ground | cream |
| Density | dense, about 620 characters |
| Media | none |
| Focal | item at 16px against a 64px headline (ratio 0.25) |

## Why it holds together

Deliberately tiny. No single item is the point; the shape of the cloud is. A hero item here would break the claim that these were all scored the same way.

## Deviations from the traced source

| What | Source | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| palette | blue and purple pills, outside the brand palette | navy and orange-700 | The source was built outside the system. Reproducing off-brand colour to be faithful would be faithful to a mistake. |
| index family label | comp-matrix-2x2 | continuous scatter | A 2x2 sorts into four named boxes; this plots continuously. Building the labelled thing would have left the real gap open. |

## What the consumer supplies

Copy only. The geometry is measured off a real slide, so when you rebuild it in Claude Design Slides keep the positions and sizes in the preview exactly: change the words, not the grid. Build the text and shapes from the Elements cards, each of which ends with its Slides recipe.

## Origin

Traced from `bank:32` and shipped as canon template `comp-priority-scatter`. In the repository its template, `wpp-es-html-deck/canon/templates/comp-priority-scatter.html`, is refreshed from this card's preview, and its trace sources (spec, measurements and reference image) are in `authoring/canon-src/comp-priority-scatter/`.

# ComparisonV1

Two approaches side by side, bridged by a motif. Archetype `compare`; about 287 characters of copy, 387 at most.

## When to use it

Before and after, or two approaches.

## Related

For tensions rather than a binary choice, use NarrativeTensionSpectrum (traced): two boxes force a binary a tension does not have.

## What the consumer supplies

The copy, inside the capacity below. Build the slide from the Elements cards (Headline, Subhead, BodyCopy, Pill, DotBullet and the rest), each of which ends with its recipe for Claude Design Slides, and take this layout's own positions and sizes from the preview. A measurement no Elements card gives is in `components/bundle.css`, under the class the preview uses. Over the maximum, pick a lower-density layout or split the slide; never set the type smaller.
